newsitem.title: USA: MSRB warns dealers about compliance with rule G-36.
newsitem.headline: MSRB warns dealers about compliance with rule G-36.

text.p: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board is warning dealers this week that enforcement agencies will step in if some dealers continue to send official statements to the board late, an advanced copy of the board's quarterly report to dealers says.

"It has come to the board's attention that some dealers are not sending official statements to the board in a timely manner," according to a notice in MSRB Reports, which is expected to reach dealers this week.

"If the board continues to receive official statements late, it will be necessary for the enforcement agencies to undertake additional action to ensure compliance with (MSRB) rule G-36," the board's one-page notice says.

Rule G-36 requires managing underwriters that are subject to the Securities and Exchange Commission's muni disclosure Rule 15c2-12 to send copies of official statements for primary offerings to the board, if an official statement was prepared.

Underwriters must deliver the documents within one business day after they get final official statements from issuers, but no later than 10 business days after final agreements to buy, offer or sell bonds, MSRB's notice says.
MSRB's notice also reminds dealers what to do when an OS has been prepared in a primary offering that is not covered by SEC's Rule 15c2-12.
In that case, rule G-36 requires dealers to send OSs to the board within one business day after the issuer delivers the securities to the dealer, MSRB's notice says.
That requirement does not apply to limited placements that are exempt from Rule 15c2-12, MSRB notes.
The board said it is reminding dealers of G-36's requirements so that official statements are accessible to the market as soon as possible after the date issues are sold.
